status: Preregistered in Stage 1, before any Iteration 3 session. Cases, rules and thresholds must not be changed after results are seen; a change requires a new protocol_version and new sessions.
reference_note: Targets are instructed fixation points shown to the participant. No independent eye tracker measures where the participant actually looked, so every spatial value is a target-referenced gaze error, not ground-truth eye-direction error.
hash_rule: Sessions record the SHA-256 of this file's bytes after converting CRLF to LF. The analyzer recomputes it the same way and rejects sessions whose hash differs.

primary.predictor: Personal nine-point calibration GazeModel, completed in the current tracking run and verified against the saved calibration before the run starts

live_preview.role: secondary; reported separately and never combined with blind results, because a visible pointer can change where the participant looks

initial.requirement: each session after a fresh nine-point calibration

collection_plan.additional_participants: Optional. Added later with this unchanged protocol; their sessions are appended, never overwriting earlier ones.

coordinates.frame: Full-display normalized coordinates: x = screen_x_px / display_width_px, y = screen_y_px / display_height_px, where the display size is DisplaySpace.bounds (WindowManager.maximumWindowMetrics on API 30+, Display.getRealSize below). The same basis is used for calibration anchors, evaluation targets and predictions.
coordinates.origin: Top-left of the display. Positive x = right, positive y = down.
coordinates.target_drawing: A target at (x, y) is drawn at view-local (x * display_width - view_left, y * display_height - view_top), where view_left/top is the evaluation view's on-screen location.
coordinates.raw_output: GazeSample.rawPoint: predictor output before filtering. Unclamped.
coordinates.final_output: GazeSample.point: GazeStabilizer output used by interaction logic. Unclamped; finite off-screen values are kept. This is the primary measured coordinate.
coordinates.display_output: Pointer rendering clamps each axis to [0.015, 0.985] (PointerDisplay in DotOverlay.kt). Logged for reference only; never used for error metrics.

timing.order: Pass 1: serpentine from the top-left (even rows left to right, odd rows right to left). Pass 2: pass 1 reversed.
timing.assignment: Each processing attempt is assigned to a presentation and phase by its frame-acceptance timestamp (SystemClock.uptimeMillis) relative to the run start, never by the target on screen when its result arrives.
timing.clock: SystemClock.uptimeMillis (monotonic) for schedule, acceptance and result times; System.nanoTime (monotonic) for durations.

validity.valid_measurement_sample: A measurement-phase attempt with outcome 'processed', quality TRACKING and finite final x and y.
validity.invalid_attempts: Kept in availability accounting with their actual outcome or quality. Excluded from spatial metrics; never imputed, carried forward or treated as zero error.
validity.off_screen: Finite final coordinates outside [0, 1] on either axis remain in every spatial metric. Their fraction is reported.
validity.settling: Settling-phase attempts are excluded from spatial, availability and throughput metrics and reported separately.

data_sufficiency.purpose: Technical eligibility for diagnostic spatial summaries. Distinct from, and looser than, the performance pass conditions.
data_sufficiency.min_eligible_fraction_note: The p95-presentation-error and mean-jitter criteria are INSUFFICIENT_DATA when fewer than ceil(0.8 * planned) presentations are technically eligible (26 of 32). The fraction reuses the predeclared 0.80 successful-presentation rate.

performance_criteria.note: Predeclared Iteration 3 prototype engineering targets. They are not evidence of reliable small-button selection. Comparisons use unrounded values.

session_criteria.definition: Successful presentations / all planned presentations in the run (32).
Nearest-rank p95 (k = ceil(0.95 * n)) of the per-presentation mean final errors of technically eligible presentations. Not a p95 across camera samples.
Mean over technically eligible presentations of sqrt(mean((x - mean_x)^2 + (y - mean_y)^2)) of valid final coordinates.
Valid measurement attempts / all measurement-phase processing attempts. Undefined (INSUFFICIENT_DATA) when there are no attempts.
Valid measurement samples / planned measurement-window time of the run (32 x 1.5 s = 48 s). A window without attempts contributes zero samples.

Nearest-rank p95 of per-attempt processing latency over all run attempts with a measured latency, including invalid, stale and discarded results. Latency runs from frame acceptance for processing to publication (or explicit discard) of its result on the main thread. Not FaceLandmarker inference time alone, not physical eye-to-display latency, not dwell time.

metric_definitions.spatial_error_norm: e = sqrt((pred_x - target_x)^2 + (pred_y - target_y)^2) in full-display normalized units. Not a percentage of the screen diagonal and not a visual angle.
metric_definitions.spatial_error_px: e_px = sqrt(((pred_x - target_x) * display_width_px)^2 + ((pred_y - target_y) * display_height_px)^2).
metric_definitions.presentation_mean_error: Mean of the spatial errors of a presentation's valid measurement samples.
metric_definitions.session_mean_error: Mean of presentation mean errors; each technically eligible presentation weighted equally.
metric_definitions.jitter_rms: sqrt(mean((x - mean_x)^2 + (y - mean_y)^2)) within one presentation; pixel version scales dx by width and dy by height.
metric_definitions.bias: Signed mean of (pred - target) per axis per presentation; session value is the mean over eligible presentations. Positive x = right, positive y = down.
metric_definitions.off_screen_fraction: Valid measurement samples with a final coordinate outside [0, 1] / all valid measurement samples.
metric_definitions.nearest_rank_p95: The k-th smallest value with k = ceil(0.95 * n), computed in integer arithmetic.

statuses.MET: The criterion was measured and satisfied its threshold.
statuses.NOT_MET: The criterion was measured and failed its threshold.
statuses.NOT_MEASURED: No session data exists for the criterion yet.
statuses.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: Data exist but are too few, or fail an integrity check, to evaluate the criterion.
statuses.INCOMPLETE: The session ended before all presentations were shown; it cannot receive a passing verdict.

assertions: Invalid or insufficient presentations cannot be successful presentations.
Missing coordinates never become zero error.
An incomplete session's verdict is INCOMPLETE, whatever its partial metrics.
A session with logging loss, unassigned rows or a checksum mismatch has verdict INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
A session verdict is MET only if every session criterion is MET.
Session p95 values are never averaged; a participant-level p95 is recomputed from pooled presentation means.

aggregation.session: All criteria are evaluated per session.
aggregation.participant: Within one compatibility group, using complete sessions only. Verdict MET only if every included session verdict is MET; NOT_MET if any is NOT_MET; INCOMPLETE if no complete session exists; otherwise INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Descriptive participant metrics weight presentations equally (successful-presentation rate, pooled-presentation p95, mean jitter) or sessions equally (availability, valid sample rate); latency is reported as the worst session p95, never as an averaged p95.
aggregation.compatibility_group: Sessions are only summarized together when mode, protocol hash, build commit and dirty flag, predictor kind, device model and display size and rotation all match.
aggregation.frame_weighting: No summary weights sessions by camera frame count.
